title: Comparison of derived functors computed on resolving models
statement: Let A be an abelian category with a derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], D a triangulated category, and F:K(A)→D a triangulated shift-compatible functor. Let P be a class of homotopy objects such that every X admits a quasi-isomorphism Y→X with Y in P. If L1,L2:D(A)→D admit natural transformations Qh⋙Lj→F whose components are invertible on P, then L1 and L2 are naturally isomorphic.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, dual part; universal property in Tag 05S9 and equation-everywhere; exactness in Tag 05SE

proof.text: Naturality of the first comparison, and its invertibility on P, show that F inverts quasi-isomorphisms between P objects. Apply the resolving-class theorem to construct a universal derived pair L with counit invertible on P.

For each j the universal property gives a transformation Lj→L. Its factorization equation shows that its components on P are invertible. Resolve any X by Y in P. Naturality along the localized resolution shows that the component at Qh(X) is invertible. Essential surjectivity of Qh makes the whole transformation an isomorphism. Compose the first transformation with the inverse of the second.

theorem nonempty_iso_of_resolving_models
    (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A]
    (D : Type uD) [Category.{vD} D] [Preadditive D] [HasZeroObject D]
    [HasShift D ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive]
    [Pretriangulated D] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D]
    (F : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ) ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (P : Set (HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ)))
    (hres : ∀ X : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ),
      ∃ (Y : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ)) (s : Y ⟶ X),
        Y ∈ P ∧ HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ) s)
    (L₁ L₂ : DerivedCategory A ⥤ D)
    (α₁ : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L₁ ⟶ F)
    (α₂ : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L₂ ⟶ F)
    (h₁ : ∀ X, X ∈ P → IsIso (α₁.app X))
    (h₂ : ∀ X, X ∈ P → IsIso (α₂.app X)) : Nonempty (L₁ ≅ L₂)
